Subject: Clarify: do you ever use our content to train models? plus retention windows

Hi Irene,

Our legal/compliance team wants a short statement we can add to section 3.2 of the MSA and a separate table with retention windows. Could you share the recommended wording and any caveats we need to surface (e.g., aggregated telemetry, emergency restores, private deployment differences)?

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front, then a short clause and a retention table below. I attached a one-page data map and a short log excerpt to illustrate what we store.

Short answers:
- Training: Redwood does not use Customer Content to train or improve models for hosted inference unless the customer explicitly opts in via a written agreement. We treat API request content, file uploads, prompt/response pairs, and embeddings as Customer Content.
- Exceptions: Aggregated, de-identified telemetry (e.g., call volumes, error rates, anonymized latency distributions) may be used to improve platform reliability; this is not tied back to individual Customer Content. Any use of customer-provided data for research or model training is opt-in and goes through legal & privacy review.
- Retention: default windows below, with contract-level customizations available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Suggested MSA clause (draft):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any production models used for inference, except where Customer has explicitly opted in via a separate, written agreement. Redwood may collect aggregated and de-identified platform telemetry for service improvement; such telemetry will not contain Customer Content or identifiers that reasonably enable re-identification of Customer data."

Retention table (default):
- API request payloads (Customer Content): retained for 30 days and then deleted from active logs and caches.
- Inference traces & debugging logs (may include redacted request identifiers, not full payloads): retained for 30 days by default; can be shortened via contract.
- Billing & usage records (token counts, billing metadata): retained for 90 days for invoicing reconciliation, archived longer per contractual terms.
- Audit logs (security events, admin actions): retained 365 days by default.
- Backups / DR snapshots: retained up to 90 days in immutable form for disaster recovery; customers may request earlier deletion and we will make reasonable efforts to remove snapshots sooner where possible.

Notes and caveats:
- Immutable backup copies and legal holds: deletion requests remove active copies; immutable backup slices may persist for a limited DR window (up to 90 days) depending on storage medium. We will document any such windows in the order form.
- Private deployments: by default Customer manages storage and keys; Redwood's control plane has no access to Customer Content unless explicitly granted.
- Verification: we provide exportable deletion receipts and can coordinate an audit (SOC2 or on-site review) as part of enterprise contracts.

I've attached: redwood-data-map.pdf (one-page map showing where different classes of data live) and log-excerpt.txt (sanitized snippet showing field names and retention tags). Please review and let me know if you want tighter windows or alternate wording. Once you confirm, I'll route to Legal for final sign-off.

Best,
Irene

Nice draft — a few precision edits for MSA-safe language and operational notes you should include in the appendix (we can add as schedule):

Proposed contract-safe sentence (short form):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve production or research models used to serve Customer, except where Customer has provided explicit, written consent."

Operational clarifications to include in a schedule (bullet form):
- "Aggregated telemetry" = metrics and anonymized counts where no Customer identifiers or content are preserved; examples included.
- Debug traces: redact full request payloads by default; traces store request IDs and error stacks for 30 days to support incident investigation.
- Backups/DR: snapshots are retained up to 90 days; for customers who require shorter windows, we will include a shorter retention SLA in the order form.
- Immutable storage & legal holds: we will notify Customer if an immutable copy subject to legal hold may prevent immediate deletion; typical recovery/retention windows for immutable objects are up to 90 days.
- Private / VPC: Customer data remains in Customer-managed storage and keys; Redwood does not have access to unencrypted Customer Content unless explicit cross-account access is configured.

Evidence and verification: recommend we attach a short export flow: customer deletion request -> ticket -> deletion receipt -> verification export (CSV) within 48 hours. That satisfies many procurement teams.

One more note: billing records retained for reconciliation should be represented as aggregated billing metadata; we keep full billing metadata for 90 days then archive per contract. If Acme needs longer archival retention for tax/regulatory reasons, we'll include it in the order form.

I think this is good to send to Rajiv with the edited wording. Grace, any redlines on wording?

- Vivek
